model_annotations.Bulgarian: Диаграмата илюстрира зависимостта между разредеността (Sparsity Rate) и перплекситета (Perplexity) за два различни модела, обозначени като „Per-Layer“ и „Per-Sequence“. По хоризонталната ос са представени стойности на разредеността, изразени в проценти, със стойности от 10% до 80% с интервал от 10%. Вертикалната ос представлява перплекситета, измерен в логаритмична скала, със стойности от 1 до 1000, като е използвана логаритмична скала, което се вижда от равномерно разпределените деления (1, 10, 100, 1000). За всяка стойност на разредеността са изобразени два стълба – син със светла сянка, представляващ „Per-Sequence“, и оранжев, представляващ „Per-Layer“. Стълбовете са групирани по стойности на разредеността, като всеки групирани стълба са разположени под съответната отметка на хоризонталната ос. Визуално се забелязва, че перплекситетът на двата модела расте с увеличаване на разредеността, като стойностите на „Per-Layer“ са системно по-високи от тези на „Per-Sequence“ при всички стойности на разредеността, освен при 10% и 20%, където двете стойности са почти равни. Най-високите стойности на перплекситет са при 80% разреденост, където стълбът на „Per-Layer“ достига над 1000, а стълбът на „Per-Sequence“ е около 500.
model_annotations.Chinese: The bar chart compares the perplexity of two models, labeled "Per-Layer" (orange) and another model (blue), across different sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The x-axis represents the sparsity rate, with categories labeled as percentages (10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%) and arranged in ascending order from left to right. The y-axis, labeled "Perplexity," uses a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at 10^0 (1), 10^1 (10), 10^2 (100), and 10^3 (1000). For each sparsity rate, two adjacent bars are displayed: the blue bar for the non-labeled model and the orange bar for the "Per-Layer" model. At sparsity rates of 10% and 20%, both models exhibit low perplexity values, with the blue model at approximately 1 and the orange model slightly higher, around 2. As the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity for both models generally increases. At 30% sparsity, both models have a perplexity of about 1. At 40% and 50% sparsity, the perplexity for both models is approximately 2. At 60% sparsity, the blue model has a perplexity of about 5, while the "Per-Layer" model has a perplexity of about 7. At 70% sparsity, the blue model's perplexity is around 15, and the "Per-Layer" model's is approximately 40. At 80% sparsity, the blue model's perplexity is approximately 500, while the "Per-Layer" model's perplexity is significantly higher, reaching nearly 1000. The "Per-Layer" model consistently shows higher perplexity than the blue model at sparsity rates of 60% and above, with the gap widening as sparsity increases. The legend in the top-left corner identifies the blue bar as the non-labeled model and the orange bar as "Per-Layer." The bars are arranged in a grouped format, with each pair of bars corresponding to a single sparsity rate. There is no visual emphasis such as shading or outlines on any of the bars.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between perplexity and sparsity rate for two different models, labeled "Per-Per" and "Per-Layer", with the y-axis representing perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³, and the x-axis showing the sparsity rate in increments from 10% to 80%. The chart contains two sets of bars for each sparsity rate: a blue bar for the "Per-Per" model and an orange bar for the "Per-Layer" model. The perplexity values for both models increase as the sparsity rate increases. At each sparsity level, the perplexity of the "Per-Layer" model is consistently higher than that of the "Per-Per" model. For instance, at a 10% sparsity rate, both models have a perplexity of approximately 1. At a 80% sparsity rate, the perplexity for the "Per-Per" model is approximately 500, while for the "Per-Layer" model it is approximately 1000. The bars are arranged in groups of two for each sparsity rate, with the "Per-Per" model's bar on the left and the "Per-Layer" model's bar on the right. The chart shows a clear upward trend in perplexity for both models as sparsity increases, with the "Per-Layer" model exhibiting a steeper increase.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm zeigt die Perplexität in Abhängigkeit von der Sparsitätsrate, wobei die Daten für zwei verschiedene Modelle oder Konfigurationen – „Per-Layer“ (dargestellt durch orangefarbene Balken) und ein zweites Modell (dargestellt durch blau-graue Balken) – verglichen werden. Die horizontale Achse stellt die Sparsitätsrate in Prozent dar, mit Werten von 10% bis 80% in 10%-Schritten, und ist als kategoriale Achse mit einer linearen Skala in logarithmischer Darstellung beschriftet. Die vertikale Achse repräsentiert die Perplexität und verwendet eine logarithmische Skala, die von 10⁰ (1) bis 10³ (1000) reicht, mit Beschriftungen bei 10⁰, 10¹, 10² und 10³. Für jede Sparsitätsrate sind zwei nebeneinander stehende Balken dargestellt, wobei der orangefarbene Balken der „Per-Layer“-Gruppe und der blau-graue Balken der anderen Gruppe entspricht. Die Balken sind in der Reihenfolge der Sparsitätsrate von links nach rechts angeordnet. Die Höhe der Balken variiert mit der Sparsitätsrate, wobei die Perplexität in beiden Gruppen mit zunehmender Sparsitätsrate ansteigt. Bei einer Sparsitätsrate von 80% erreichen beide Balken die höchste Höhe, wobei der orangefarbene Balken („Per-Layer“) eine höhere Perplexität als der blau-graue Balken aufweist. Bei 10% Sparsitätsrate sind die Balken am kürzesten, wobei der blau-graue Balken eine geringfügig höhere Perplexität als der orangefarbene aufweist. Die Legende befindet sich oben links und identifiziert die beiden Balkenfarben mit den entsprechenden Modellbezeichnungen.
